LossConvertToTerron:
Your personal matrix was successfully replaced with 3B-level matrix. Initially you were taking part in full-scale battles. Several times you got yourself killed, but each time they managed to restore your matrix. Then the Coalition forces moved into a full-scale offensive, using you as a human bomb. Disguised as a ranger, you infiltrated the Galactic Council and self-destroyed. Left without higher command, the Coalition forces surrendered all of their key points within days, while you were promoted to level 1A...
The war went on for a long time, but the terronoids were the only species to survive. Terron moved on to the next target -- the neighboring part of the Galaxy -- resulting in a new war with Makhpella. Being a high priority machine, you were promoted to protoforming wing chief and were not actively engaged in the hostilities that followed.
LossConvertToTerron1:
Your personal matrix was replaced to a terronoid analogue of series 0-1P. Having analyzed your intellectual development coefficient, your brain was extracted from your body, placed in the brain section of a powerful equantor and reinforced together with your equals. In close collaboration with the brains of other ex-rangers, you concluded that you could liberate yourselves from this slavery. Together with two other individuals you reprogrammed the onboard computer and hijacked a terronoid cruiser.
Having run out of fuel, you made it to the nearest accessible star system. The cruiser was escorted to land on one of the local planets. There was a trial, where all members of the Galactic Council, save for the fae, voted to have the traitors executed. The maloqs wanted to crush the defendants with their bare hands, the pelengs called for execution by drowning, humans voted for electrical incineration, while the gaals favored toxic injection. And only the faeyan representatives proposed to use the brains for experiments.
One can only guess as to how it all would have ended had it not been for the victory over the dominators. While everyone else was celebrating, the fae stole the equantor and integrated all of the traitors' brain lobes into a deep-sea cyborg animal. The animal was then released on a unpopulated planet and is presently being studied.
LossConvertToTerron2:
The process of replacing your personal identity matrix was completed with errors, resulting in your life cycle as a machine ending a mere two days after inception. Terron saw no point in rehabilitating the broken matrix, so your body was sealed in a capsule and launched into open space. Soon you were discovered by a military patrol. Seeking to hide the awful fact of the betrayal of a famous ranger, the capsule was towed into a black hole.
The ranger's corpse drifted in hyperspace for some time before the capsule was spotted by pirates and the wire-ridden body was extracted. Once your identify was ascertained, the bandits were overjoyed and decided to immortalize the great traitor for posterity. The contents of Ranger 's scull cavity were replaced with a microchip. For a time you served as a mechanical statue, greeting guests in the vacuum space of the pirate base.
The Coalition won the war against the dominators, but the post-war Galaxy was instantly overrun with pirate clans who had been biding their time, waiting for the opportunity to make a power play. The five races were forced to resign themselves to the new state of affairs and abide by the laws of the underworld. The body of Ranger became a symbol of infamy and betrayal, highly valued by the new authorities. Today, all pirate bases feature a replica of your mechanical statue, welcoming arrivals.
LossConvertToTerron3:
As your personal identity matrix was being replaced there was a short circuit, but Terron paid no attention and went ahead with the process. Together with other remade pilots, you were assigned to combat ships. Over time sections of your brain started malfunctioning: communication was the first to go, followed by will and finally reasoning. As a result, you were no longer capable of executing the server's commands.
It is known that terronoids exercise only one solution to personal matrix malfunctions: complete erasure of the broken intellectual unit. Realizing this, you miraculously escaped the hostile robots by the skin of your teeth and proceeded to spend the remainder of your life in solitude, your combat power occasionally spilling out onto meteors and passing ships unfortunate enough to wander into this remote corner of the Galaxy.
The dominators defeated the Coalition forces with the help of their new weapon, the planetary destructor, eliminating organic life on all known populated planets. Thus this spiral arm of the Galaxy ended its existence in the cold grip of the dominators.

WinPirate10:
Having left the ranks of space rangers, you headed to the nearest pirate base and took command of the the pirate clan. Of course, this decision meant you had to relinquish all the perks and privileges due to every veteran who bravely fought for the Coalition.

In return you were given the chance to bring back the times of "pirate romanticism," a task you accomplished brilliantly. Thanks to you, the word of a noble pirate once again rang loud and true across the Galaxy!

Despite your contentious reputation, you managed to live a long and happy life, commanding great respect among not only your brothers-in-arms, but also their enemies. Tales of your courage and sense of justice became the stuff of legend, passing from generation to generation via not only the latest technologies, but just as they would in the good old times: from a human to a maloq, from a maloq to a peleng, and from a peleng -- for a reasonable fee, to be sure -- to the rest of the world.
WinPirate11:
You have made the most important decision in your life, evolving from a free space wanderer to a pirate politician -- the baron of a ruling clan.

The pirates sacrificed a great deal in the ruthless war against the dominators. Millions of lives were lost, far outweighing even the ongoing strife against the Coalition. This greatly undermined the pirate leadership's reputation, including yours. Fortunately, you quickly figured out which way the wind blows and framed several high-ranking khans, letting them take the hit for the battle losses.

After the robot war was over, you launched a large-scale campaign to restore the worlds ravaged by the war, tapping funds from those planets that were beyond help. Your strategy worked, and though several Galactic sectors ended up being downright unlivable, others were restored to levels of prosperity of the Coalition era.

Unfortunately, not everybody supported your actions, and on the ten year anniversary of winning the war you were assassinated by an unidentified sniper. According to the official report, the shooter was a citizen from one of the worlds you devastated. Despite dying young, you have secured a historical legacy as one of the brightest personalities from the war years.
WinPirate12:
You celebrated your entry into the world of politics with a bang, and when the hangover wore off you set out to deal with matters of great importance, alongside other pirate activists. Naturally, your authority was unquestioned, and your voice carried the weight of three. Other pirates respected you for the knowledge gained in your time as a ranger. Hard as it is to imagine, certain pirate capos and even khans held only the loosest grip on sciences like mathematics and even astronomy. Your patience quickly wearing thin, you instituted compulsory training courses to improve the pirates' erudition under the tutelage of top faeyan specialists. This decision ended up serving the Galaxy well when all these slackers became rulers of various planets and formed the Pirate Council of the five races.

Now a top commander, you never again took the helm of a ship, traveling the Galaxy on luxury liners instead. And only the select few knew that you have kept your trusty old combat ship in a safe place, dropping by for the occasional visit to reminisce about the good old times.

WinPirate14:
Upon parking your trusty ship for good, you began the organizational efforts for the good of the pirate clan. Though you never did become a pirate baron, your experience as a ranger proved invaluable in pulling off various ambitious projects, starting from one pirate planet and ending with the entire star sector.

Fourteen years after you've exchanged a pilot's cockpit for a paper-laden office table, you were nominated for the post of planetary ruler. You scored a resounding victory on election day, garnering overwhelming support. Upon making it to the top, you remained there until your retirement, eventually surrendering your chair to a young and promising up-and-comer. After stepping down, you proceeded to spend many a long winter night telling your grandkids about your adventures fighting the dominators, as well as hundreds of other fascinating stories from your rich ranger past.
WinPirate15:
Your contribution to victory against the dominators was substantial. As a result, you became the public's darling. For several years following the war, your face was a staple on stereovision and in newspapers, and a few books were even written about your ranger career. You constantly received invitations to become a showman or a politician. It didn't take you long to realize that it was essentially the same profession, only with different titles. You fielded every offer of this type with a polite yet firm refusal.

Once peace was firmly established in your arm of the Galaxy, the ranger core was disbanded with honors. A grand ceremony was organized for the occasion, at which all of the war's participants were awarded. You were nabbed to host the event, which ended up being a wonderful time. You were especially glad to see your former companions with whom you had braved many a battle.

Most of the former rangers returned to civilian life. As for the others, who were particularly restless, you proposed to resume your collaboration by founding a new elite security agency. In only a few short years your firm and its quality of service became the stuff of legend throughout the Galaxy, bringing you more business than you could hope to handle. No pirates or extremists could match the skill of your brave companions and former Coalition fighters. Though financial security arrived at almost the very beginning of your new career, you kept working as the company head to a ripe old age, ultimately retiring an extraordinarily respected person.
WinPirate16:
If not for your support, it's doubtful that the pirates could have beaten the dominators on their own. Indeed, it was their great fortune that a skilled fighter such as yourself was on their side. Alas, not all bandits supported your opposition, with many opting to hide in the rear, but those that followed you proved enough to bring the entire Galaxy back into pirate hands.

Once the dominator threat was destroyed, you suddenly found yourself without a job. With no more enemies left to fight and all of your associates from the pirate clan settled in political posts, the younger pirate generation quickly forgot who it was that had saved them from swarms of ruthless robots. After spending a few eventful years in bars, getting sloshed and telling war tales, you realized the futility of your behavior and decided to retire from the grind of modern life. After choosing an unpopulated planet with a habitable though not entirely hospitable climate, you built yourself a home in the bosom of nature, growing food in your own private garden and fishing from a nearby lake.

Many years into your new reclusive life you spied a spaceship in the sky. Nursing a vague but unrelenting anxiety, you decided to hide in the nearby woods just in case. The visitors were a bunch of goons who burned your hut to the ground for the hell of it, broke all the equipment and trampled the entire garden. Unable to endure their defiling the fruits of your labor, you grabbed a heavy stick and ran over to the house. Thanks to your athletic shape and unforgotten ranger skills, you proceeded to give the punks a good thrashing and were within an inch of winning... But then a shot rang out. One of the bandits was armed.

They threw your body into the fire and ran off.

It wasn't until several decades later that the Galaxy learned of your fate, having discovered your ship hidden in the woods. Your favorite meadow has since become a popular pilgrimage site, with a monument to your heroic deeds erected right in the middle.
WinPirate17:
If not for your support, it's doubtful that the pirates could have beaten the dominators on their own. Indeed, it was their great fortune that a skilled fighter such as yourself was on their side. Alas, not all bandits supported your opposition, with many opting to hide in the rear, but those that followed you proved enough to bring the entire Galaxy back into pirate hands.

What happened then to the arm of the Galaxy populated by the five races could probably be viewed as the most comical time in the history of the known universe, if not for the countless victims of said mad events. Part of the blame lay squarely on your shoulders, as it was you who, before defeating the dominators, had terminated the pirate leader who had been pushing for the integration of the pirate clan with the highest rungs of the Coalition hierarchy. In so doing you brought back the era of pirate outlaws, with each pirate answering to no higher authority and acting without any regard for others. Provisional pirate governments, established in the course of opposing the dominators, rushed to secure their grip on power the moment the robot enemy was no more, while various pirate capos and khans vied against them, anxious to take their turn at the helm of whole planets.

The upshot of all this bedlam was that in a few short years the various planetary governments quarreled with one another over race, politics, morality, religion and every other issue imaginable, leading to an all-out war. Relations between maloqs and pelengs became especially volatile, and nothing could keep the two races from getting at each other's throats. The virtually unheard of religious cult known as Game Developers of Dawn strode into public eye by capturing an entire star system, then migrating everybody, people and planets and all, to a different arm of the Galaxy.

In the early stages of the chaos you tried your best to talk sense into all the parties and calm the situation. Upon realizing the futility of your efforts, you gave up and settled on one of the primitive agrarian planets undisturbed by war and uprisings, not even news of the madness that had overtaken the Galaxy. It was there that you lived out the rest of your days, leaving this world a decrepit bag of bones. Many centuries later, when peace finally returned to the Galaxy, the historians honored you with a dubious title -- the lamest hero in the history of the Galaxy.
WinPirate18:
Upon defeating the dominators, you garnered your share of glory. However, putting your face on screens all over the Galaxy led to your ship being attacked by a well-organized group of pirate assassins mere days later. By pure miracle you managed to survive the attack. Realizing that the pirates would never leave be the one who had exposed their wicked plans and beheaded their organization, you knew that you had but one choice -- to disappear. The Coalition special forces staged an accident in which your ship collided with a large asteroid, followed by a grand funeral for the hero of the Coalition, the broadcast of which you watched on stereovision.

With new documents and a new identity, as well as a healthy bank account, destiny was yours to decide. You could have spent the rest of your days on the Galaxy's finest interstellar resorts. Or you could have accepted the job offer from the Coalition's Intelligence Agency and become instructor for a new generation of special agents. You could have even started on a memoir in the style of a sci-fi novel or learned to play an ancient human instrument called the accordion...

But, as it happens, one day you found yourself standing outside a military training facility, your eyes fixed on a poster: "The Galaxy Needs Space Rangers!" It felt as though your decision was made for you then and there...
WinPirate5:
Once again you accepted an offer you couldn't refuse. By agreeing to lead the pirate forces you severed all remaining ties with your past, in which you were a space ranger and one of the Galaxy's heroes. The command wrote you off as a casualty and paid your family a settlement of cr.

You became quite the power player in your new life, working toward integrating the pirate clan with official authorities. Making shrewd use of all manner of tools to achieve your goals, including bribery, blackmail and assassination, you were nearly successful in bending the Coalition leadership to your will. On the verge of becoming a true "grey eminence," the unofficial emperor of the Galaxy, your claim to ultimate authority was denied by the steady arm of a marksman assassin. The killer escaped, and the identity of whoever ordered the hit was never discovered.

But don't fret -- at least you made it into the Galactic Encyclopedia!
